stem.text: Grain is loaded into a silo at a rate modeled by \( E(t) = 2 \sin{\left(\frac{t^{2}}{2} \right)} + 8 \) tons per hour and is unloaded from it at a rate modeled by \( L(t) = \cos{\left(\frac{t}{2} \right)} + 3 \) tons per hour, for \( 0 \le t \le 4 \), where t is measured in hours. At time t = 0 the silo holds 85 tons. Using a calculator, find the amount in the silo at time t = 4. Show the setup for the calculation, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The net rate is inflow minus outflow, \( E(t) - L(t) \), so the answer is \( 85 + \int_{0}^{4} \left(E(t) - L(t)\right)\,dt \).
worked_solution.rule_named: net rate as inflow minus outflow

worked_solution.text: With a calculator in radian mode, \( \int_{0}^{4} \left(E(t) - L(t)\right)\,dt \) is approximately 19.996 (more places are kept).
Adding the initial amount gives about 104.996 tons.

options.derivation: L(t) substituted without parentheses, so only its constant term is subtracted and its cosine term is added
the inflow and outflow rates added instead of subtracted
the integral of the net rate reported as the amount, with the initial 85 tons left out
